subject: KiteFin inference cost discovery — recap + next steps
body:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@kitefin.com>, Procurement <procurement@kitefin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: KiteFin inference cost discovery — recap + next steps

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so everyone's aligned.

High-level pain / goals you shared:
- Token-level cost pressure: current spend for batch processing and streaming prompts is outpacing projected revenue for Q3.
- Peak latency SLAs: customer-facing flows need sub-600ms 95th for short chats (<= 128 tokens).
- Predictability for procurement: want a deterministic pricing piece for budgeting (reserved capacity interest).

Current stack and constraints:
- Backend: in-house microservices on AWS (EKS) calling a mix of open LLMs and one paid provider.
- Serving: custom shim that currently does no KV prefix caching; batching is per-request at the app layer.
- Hardware: mostly spot instances for dev, on-demand for production; no dedicated GPU pool.

Success criteria you defined:
1) Reduce cost-per-1k tokens by at least 30% while maintaining quality.
2) Hit 95th latency < 600ms for chat endpoints at expected Q3 traffic (projected ~120 rps peak).
3) Procurement sign-off with a clear reserved-capacity quote + SLA by the end of May.

Redwood observations and initial recommendations (from our side):
- Batching & caching: substantial wins available by moving prefix/KV caching into the serving runtime and enabling continuous batching for burst smoothing.
- Quantization: you're open to 4-bit for non-sensitive models; recommend scoped A/B on 4-bit quantized variant for throughput tests.
- Routing: mix of cheaper model variants for background tasks + low-latency variants for chat will help meet both cost and latency goals.

Action items / next steps
1) Redwood: share a one-page Mutual Action Plan (attached) and a preliminary cost estimate with two scenarios (conservative reserved + aggressive batch/caching uplift) — attachment: redwood-cost-estimate-quant-batches.xlsx — by EOD Thursday.
2) KiteFin: provide sample traffic profile + 24-hour token histogram and a sanitized example prompt set for quality checks (ideally by next Tue).
3) Technical runbook: schedule a 60-min infra deep-dive with Dev Patel and your infra lead to validate batching feasibility (suggested window: next Wed 10–12 PT).

If that matches your view, I'll lock in the MAP and send a calendar invite for the infra deep-dive.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134


From: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@kitefin.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@kitefin.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 18:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KiteFin inference cost discovery — recap + next steps

Jordan — thanks for the write-up, very helpful. Confirming a few points:
- We're comfortable trying quantized models for non-sensitive data; for PII flows we need plaintext routed to the higher-tier variant.
- I'll pull the 24-hr token histogram and sanitized prompts — should have those by Monday.
- Procurement wants reserved vs on-demand pricing comparisons; the MAP will be useful.

One ask: can the initial cost sheet include a rough OPEX estimate for running a dedicated GPU pool vs Redwood dedicated offering? We need to justify whether to keep infra in-house or move to dedicated.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Cheng
Head of ML Platform | KiteFin
alex.cheng@kitefin.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@kitefin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@kitefin.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 08:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KiteFin inference cost discovery — recap + next steps

Appreciate the confirmation, Alex. Yes — we'll include a 3-line OPEX comp (capex vs managed) in the estimate and outline observability differences.

I've attached the MAP (KiteFin_MAP_v1.pdf) and the preliminary cost scenarios workbook. High level:
- Scenario A (Reserved + conservative batching): ~28–35% token cost reduction; 95th latency expected to remain within 600–700ms depending on model choice and autoscaling.
- Scenario B (Aggressive batching + 4-bit quantized variants for background tasks): ~40–55% token cost reduction; expect better unit economics but will run a small quality regression test first.

Next operational step: can we get your infra lead's availability for the deep-dive? Dev, can you take point on the technical agenda and call invite?

I'll also open a HubSpot opportunity and push the MAP there for your procurement team to reference.

Best,
Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Procurement <procurement@kitefin.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@kitefin.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KiteFin inference cost discovery — recap + next steps

Jordan — Procurement received the MAP. Two quick asks: 1) Can you include a sample SLA with uptime and latency targets? 2) Do you have a standard PO template we can use?

If you can send both by EOD Friday we'll prioritize internal review.

Thanks,
Sam (on behalf of KiteFin Procurement)
